data.name: Maleek
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'm-l-k', which means 'to rule', 'to govern'. Maleek is an Arabic name meaning 'Lord', 'Master'. In Islamic history, Maleek is used as a title for a ruler or master. It is also a common name for male children in the Islamic world.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine leadership and sovereignty
data.numerology_meaning: People with the name Maleek are adventurous and independent. They are driven by a strong desire for freedom and are often unconventional in their thinking and actions. They have a strong sense of self and are not afraid to take risks.

in_urdu.name: ملک

data.cultural_impact: The name Maleek holds a significant cultural impact as it has been used as a title for Muslim rulers and emperors throughout history. `Umar ibn al-Khattab, the second caliph of Islam, is also known as Maleek al-Muslimin, or the 'Lord of Muslims'. This title emphasizes the importance of effective and just leadership in the Islamic community. It also reflects the Islamic ideal of worldly power being used for the sake of God and the betterment of people.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Maleek represents the concept of submission to God Almighty. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) taught us to submit to God’s will and be His obedient servants. By using the name Maleek, one can constantly be reminded to submit to God's rule and guidance in all aspects of life, ultimately striving for a deeper relationship with Him. The use of the title "Lord" or "Master" in connection with God is a common expression of reverence and humility towards the Creator.
